SLE Government of Canada: Second Language Evaluation

Public Service Language Training

Verbal Link Institute offers specialized English and French language training for individuals preparing for the Canadian federal public service Second Language Evaluation (SLE) exams. Our courses focus on the three official assessment components: reading comprehension, written expression, and oral interaction.

We provide preparation for A, B, and C proficiency levels and support learners seeking bilingual positions, career advancement, or language profile requirements within the Government of Canada.

Training levels

Progress, level by level

Our Public Service Language Training programs are designed to help learners progressively develop the language skills required for bilingual positions within the Canadian federal public service. We provide structured preparation for A, B, and C proficiency levels in both English and French, based on the standards used in the Government of Canada’s Second Language Evaluation (SLE) system. Each level focuses on improving communication skills in professional workplace contexts, including reading comprehension, written expression, and oral interaction.

ALevel

Level A Intermediate Proficiency

Level A is designed for learners beginning their journey toward bilingual workplace communication. At this stage, learners develop foundational English or French skills needed for simple and routine professional interactions.

Training at this level focuses on:

  • ✓ Understanding basic workplace vocabulary and instructions
  • ✓ Reading and understanding short professional texts and emails
  • ✓ Writing simple sentences and basic responses
  • ✓ Participating in short conversations and introductions
  • ✓ Building confidence in everyday workplace communication

Ideal for: individuals who are new to the language or who need to strengthen their basic communication skills before progressing further.

BLevel

Level B Intermediate Proficiency

Level B focuses on developing more independent and effective communication skills for professional environments. Learners improve their ability to understand, discuss, and respond to more complex workplace situations in English or French.

Training at this level includes:

  • ✓ Reading and interpreting longer workplace documents and reports
  • ✓ Writing structured emails, summaries, and professional responses
  • ✓ Expressing ideas clearly during discussions and meetings
  • ✓ Improving grammar, vocabulary, and fluency
  • ✓ Practicing workplace scenarios and interactive communication exercises

Suitable for: professionals who already have a working knowledge of the language and want to improve their performance and confidence in bilingual work environments.

CLevel

Level C Advanced Proficiency

Level C is intended for learners aiming for advanced professional fluency and high-level bilingual performance. This level prepares participants for complex communication tasks requiring precision, confidence, and strong comprehension skills.

Training at this level emphasizes:

  • ✓ Understanding detailed and specialized professional documents
  • ✓ Communicating fluently and accurately in formal workplace situations
  • ✓ Presenting and defending ideas clearly during discussions and meetings
  • ✓ Producing well-structured professional writing with advanced vocabulary and grammar
  • ✓ Developing spontaneous and confident oral communication skills

Ideal for: professionals pursuing leadership roles, advanced bilingual positions, or higher language profile requirements within the federal public service.

Go further

Two specialized government programs

Framework program

Public Language Training (PLF2)

PLF2 (Public Language Training Framework Level 2) is the standard reference used by federal departments to develop bilingual capacity among employees. At Verbal Link Institute, we align all training with the Canada School of Public Service (CSPS) framework, ensuring that our programs meet the linguistic, communicative, and cultural expectations of public service work.

  • ✓ Intensive PLF2 French (full-time): 20 to 25 hours per week
  • ✓ Part-time PLF2 French: 6 to 10 hours per week
  • ✓ Custom departmental sessions, tailored to ministry needs
  • ✓ English for Francophone Employees: PLF2 format equivalent
